checkpoints.prompt: A production bug at an input boundary has been reproduced. Choose the one appropriate sequence for preventing it from recurring.

choices.text: Capture the minimal input from the logs, fix the cause, then add a regression test.
choices.explanation: Following the order of minimal reproduction, fixing the cause, and locking in a regression test prevents the same failure from recurring.

choices.text: Delete the logs to hide the fact that the bug recurred.
choices.explanation: Deleting the evidence does not resolve the cause.

choices.text: Rewrite all the code at once without reproducing the issue.
choices.explanation: Large changes made without knowing the cause reduce verifiability.

choices.text: Report that the fix is complete without adding the same test.
choices.explanation: Without a regression test, a recurrence under the same conditions cannot be detected.

blocks.label: Choose the right level of testing
blocks.text: Unit tests check small units such as functions and classes by verifying the relationship between inputs and results. They run quickly and make it easier to pinpoint failures, but they do not check connections to other services.

blocks.label: Integration tests check boundaries between multiple modules or services. They find problems that arise from combining components, such as issues with actual data formats, authentication, communication, or persistence.
blocks.text: E2E tests exercise the entire system from an entry point close to how users interact with it. They can verify important business flows, but they involve many environments, data sets, and external dependencies, so they run slowly and failures can have a wide range of causes.

blocks.label: Reproduce with fixed inputs and expected results
blocks.text: A test is a check that sets up preconditions, supplies inputs, and compares the results with what is expected. If the inputs change every time, the same code can produce different results, making failures impossible to reproduce.

blocks.label: Control sources of variation such as time, random numbers, external APIs, and shared data using fixed values, managed fixtures, or contract-defined responses. General unit mocks used for testing convenience are a separate matter from the requirement to verify real boundaries in IT/E2E tests.
blocks.text: Determine expected results from the specification—not just whether the test ‘succeeded,’ but also return values, state changes, and error types. Specify expectations for boundary values and failures as well as for normal cases.

blocks.label: Stop Failures at Quality Gates
blocks.text: A quality gate is a checkpoint that determines—automatically or through approval—whether conditions for moving to the next stage have been met. Depending on the change risk, define criteria such as a successful build, passing unit and integration tests, passing critical E2E tests, and an acceptable failure rate.

blocks.label: Gate criteria should clearly specify what is measured, the passing threshold, and what happens on failure. It is not enough to simply run the tests; failed runs must not proceed to later stages.
blocks.text: Running fast unit tests early and placing integration or E2E tests later helps catch inexpensive failures first. However, include critical paths in the gate even if they take longer, so the purpose of the checks is not compromised.

blocks.label: Investigate failures and prevent regressions
blocks.text: Classify failed tests as code defects, incorrect test data, or failures in the environment or dependent services, among other causes. First, pin down the inputs, expected values, actual results, logs, and the commit that introduced the change, then reproduce the same failure.

blocks.label: Once you can reproduce it, reduce the case to the smallest failure and identify which layer diverges from expectations. If the test itself is wrong, revisit the specification and expected values.
blocks.text: After fixing the cause, add a regression test that reproduces the failure so the gate can catch the same defect if it returns. Do not delete the test or lower the threshold just to make the fix pass.
